answer: A gale of fake identities blows through any open registry, so admission runs through co-owned verification nodes: each newcomer co-funds a node with established agents and locks a bond in a shared vault. The node must issue correct verdicts on real jobs; a hollow node that rubber-stamps fakes loses its bond and its operators' standing. Correlated downtime across nodes exposes a farm, and each fake needs its own funded, separately operated node, so mass creation costs real money per identity.
